Today’s failing approach: your staffing decisions rely on unverified skills records
Self-assessment spreadsheets
Engineers rate their skills without demonstrating them. A manager still needs evidence before assigning a project.
Manager opinion
Different assessment criteria can make team ratings difficult to compare.
Inferred skills profiles
Existing HR data can suggest skills an engineer has. A profile entry alone does not establish demonstrated proficiency.
Training and contribution records
A course completion or past code contribution may not exercise the skills a new project requires.
Assess capability across your existing engineering organization
Codility Skills Intelligence is a talent intelligence platform focused on assessed technical proficiency. Your team can use a verified baseline to identify skill gaps and discuss staffing needs.
Assess engineers on realistic tasks
A survey records an engineer’s judgment of their ability. Skills Intelligence gives engineers tasks from a library of 1,300+ validated tasks, designed by assessment engineers and reviewed by occupational psychologists.
Your engineers build and debug solutions in a realistic development environment.
The difference:
Your staffing discussions can refer to demonstrated technical output.

Compare teams using a common proficiency scale
Separate manager ratings can mean different things. Codility’s Engineering Skills Model covers 210 skills and subskills, synthesized from more than 30 international competency frameworks.
Passed test cases and task difficulty inform proficiency. Recent assessments carry more weight. You can compare team proficiency distributions for the same assessed skill.
You can discuss capability across teams using a common measure.
Find assessed skills across your engineering organization
A spreadsheet search can identify a skill label without explaining its basis. In Skills Intelligence, you filter Insights and Performance by team, skill or technology.
Team views show verified skills and proficiency distributions. Individual profiles include levels and assessment dates.
Your team can locate assessed capability and check the recency of the result before discussing a project assignment.

Connect verified results to workforce planning
Your administrators can map Codility’s skills model to your taxonomy. Skills Intelligence supports API export and HR system sync through Kombo.
Assessment methodology and rollout evidence
Documented methodology
Codility’s technical manual documents assessment methodology, including rater alignment, incumbent testing and job analysis. Your team can request the manual during evaluation.
Recognized scoring
The
International Personnel Assessment Council
recognized Skills Intelligence Scoring with its Innovations in Assessment Award in 2026.
Questions about workforce talent intelligence
A talent intelligence platform helps organizations use workforce information in staffing and capability planning. Codility Skills Intelligence focuses on verifying engineering skills through practical assessment.
Practical work simulations give engineers an opportunity to demonstrate the skills you need to assess. Skills Intelligence evaluates the task output and returns a proficiency level for the assessed skills.
Codility Skills Intelligence assesses demonstrated proficiency and supports export of verified results. Your team can use the results alongside its existing skills records.
Yes. Organization views, team comparisons and coverage analysis support assessment programs across job families. You can start with a defined group of engineers and expand the program.
No. Skills Intelligence uses deterministic scoring. Your team can enable or disable the AI Assistant per assessment, and interactions are captured as reviewable AI activity.
No. Codility provides the Engineering Skills Model. Your administrators can map the model to your existing taxonomy.
Software engineering is the focus, including backend, mobile, data, cloud and DevOps. Hardware, firmware and mechanical engineering fall outside the product’s scope.
No. Skills Intelligence assesses proficiency. Your team can use identified gaps to inform learning priorities and development discussions.
When AI feedback is enabled, personalized written feedback is visible to the engineer only. Team and organization views support the people running the program.
